content.content:
1	"""Deterministic 2D grid A* planner.
2	
3	Public entry points: ``plan(width, height, blocked, start, goal, costs=None,
4	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
5	max_cost=None)``, ``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals,
6	costs=None, trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None,
7	snapshot=False, max_cost=None)``,
8	``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
9	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None)``,
10	``plan_batch(width, height, blocked, requests, costs=None, trace=False,
11	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
12	max_cost=None)``,
13	``plan_multi_start(width, height, blocked, starts, goal, costs=None,
14	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
15	max_cost=None)``,
16	``replay(width, height, blocked, start, goal, path, costs=None,
17	dynamic_blocked=None, diagnose=False)``,
18	``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)``,
19	``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None, trace=False)``
20	and
21	``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
22	trace=False)``.
23	
24	Semantics:
25	- Four-neighborhood moves, Manhattan heuristic. Without ``costs`` each step
26	  has unit cost. With ``costs`` (a height-by-width matrix of positive
27	  integers, row-major: ``costs[y][x]``) entering a cell costs that cell's
28	  value; the start cell's cost is never counted, so ``cost`` is the sum of
29	  the costs of the cells entered along the path.
30	- Tie-breaking is fully specified and order-independent: compare f, then h,
31	  then the (x, y) coordinate in lexicographic order.
32	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the nodes popped from the priority queue and
33	  closed for the first time (the goal counts when reached; stale heap
34	  entries and duplicate closings do not).
35	- Returns ``{"path": [...], "cost": int, "expanded": int}`` on success and
36	  ``{"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": int}`` when unreachable.
37	- When ``trace`` is true, both kinds of results additionally include
38	  ``expanded_nodes``: the list of coordinate tuples closed for the first
39	  time, in expansion order (includes the start, and the goal on success);
40	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. The field is omitted entirely when
41	  ``trace`` is false or omitted.
42	
43	Search budget (``max_expanded``):
44	- ``max_expanded`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key,
45	  value, exception type and validation order of the default behavior
46	  untouched. Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a
47	  bool: other types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise
48	  ``ValueError``. These checks run after all existing grid, costs,
49	  ``trace`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` validation (including the frame-0
50	  check) and before the search starts.
51	- The budget counts closed nodes (exactly what ``expanded`` counts); once
52	  the limit is reached no further node is closed. When the budget is
53	  provided the result always carries an additional ``status`` field:
54	  ``"found"`` when the goal was closed within the limit (the usual
55	  ``path``/``cost`` are returned), ``"unreachable"`` when the candidates
56	  were exhausted without reaching the goal, and ``"budget_exhausted"``
57	  when live candidates remained but the budget stopped the search (then
58	  ``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded`` is the actual closed
59	  count, at most ``max_expanded``).
60	- The budget applies identically in static and dynamic mode and never
61	  changes expansion order, path choice, trace entries or determinism: a
62	  budgeted trace is a prefix of the unbudgeted one. With ``trace=True``
63	  only actually closed nodes are recorded, so a zero budget records
64	  nothing -- even when ``start == goal`` a zero budget returns
65	  ``budget_exhausted`` with ``expanded == 0``; the single-point success
66	  result requires at least one closed node (``max_expanded >= 1``).
67	- ``replay`` is unaffected: it keeps validating candidate paths only and
68	  accepts no budget parameter.
69	
70	Cost limit (``max_cost``):
71	- ``max_cost`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key, value,
72	  exception type and validation order of the previous behavior untouched.
73	  Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a bool: other
74	  types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise ``ValueError``. The
75	  check runs after all existing grid, costs, ``trace``, ``dynamic_blocked``,
76	  ``max_expanded`` and ``snapshot`` validation and before the search
77	  starts.
78	- The limit caps the accumulated entering-cell cost of a route, measured
79	  from the start (the start cell still costs 0 and each entered cell costs
80	  its ``costs`` value, or 1 without ``costs``). A candidate whose
81	  accumulated cost would exceed the limit is discarded; a candidate at
82	  exactly the limit still competes. The limit applies identically in
83	  static mode, dynamic mode and ``plan_any``, and never changes expansion
84	  order, tie-breaks, the minimum-cost choice, the multi-goal endpoint
85	  comparison or trace entries.
86	- When ``max_cost`` is provided the result always carries ``status``:
87	  ``"found"`` on success, and on failure ``"cost_exhausted"`` when at
88	  least one candidate was discarded for exceeding the limit, otherwise
89	  ``"unreachable"`` (``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded``
90	  counts the actually closed nodes). When ``max_expanded`` is also given,
91	  a budget stop still takes priority with ``"budget_exhausted"``.
92	  ``trace`` keeps recording only actually closed nodes, and the
93	  ``start == goal`` single-point zero-cost result and the zero-budget
94	  rules are unchanged.
95	- With ``snapshot=True`` the checkpoint records the ``max_cost`` value
96	  when one was provided (and no new field when it was not). ``resume``
97	  treats a checkpoint without the field as ``None``, validates a present
98	  field with the same rules (``TypeError`` for wrong types, ``ValueError``
99	  for negative values or a state inconsistent with the limit) before any
100	  searching, and a resumed search is equivalent to one uninterrupted call
101	  with the same limit. ``replay`` accepts no ``max_cost`` parameter.
102	
103	Dynamic obstacles (``dynamic_blocked``):
104	- ``dynamic_blocked`` may be omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence, which
105	  leaves the static behavior above untouched. Otherwise it must be a
106	  sequence of frames; each frame is an iterable of grid coordinates that
107	  are blocked at that time frame. Frame 0 constrains ``start``; the
108	  coordinate at path index ``t`` must avoid both the static obstacles and
109	  frame ``t``, and frames beyond the last one reuse the last frame.
110	- Moves are still four-neighborhood only: no waiting in place and no
111	  repeated coordinates along the path. Because feasibility of a route
112	  depends on the coordinates it already visited, candidates that reach the
113	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
114	  states and are never merged: every route that satisfies the constraints
115	  can be explored. ``cost`` is still the sum of the costs of the cells
116	  entered; the start cell is never counted.
117	- The minimum-cost feasible route is returned. When total costs tie, the
118	  fixed priority is f, then h, then x, y, t, and candidates still tied are
119	  ordered lexicographically by their complete coordinate sequence, so the
120	  result never depends on the iteration order of the obstacle sets, the
121	  coordinates inside a frame, or the traversal order.
122	- In dynamic mode ``expanded_nodes`` records ``(x, y, t)`` triples in
123	  actual closing order and ``expanded`` counts closed space-time route
124	  states one per entry; a discarded candidate is never recorded. When the
125	  same ``(x, y, t)`` is closed through different histories, its triple
126	  appears once per closing in closing order, and ``expanded`` counts each
127	  such entry. On failure ``path``/``cost`` are ``None``.
128	- Validation: the outer value must be a sequence and every frame an
129	  iterable of coordinates; strings/bytes and non-two-integer coordinates
130	  raise ``TypeError``, out-of-bounds coordinates raise ``ValueError``,
131	  duplicates within a frame are merged, and a ``start`` blocked at frame 0
132	  raises ``ValueError``. All checks run before the search starts.
133	
134	Multi-goal planning (``plan_any``):
135	- ``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, ...)`` accepts the same
136	  grid, blocked, start, costs, trace, dynamic_blocked and max_expanded
137	  arguments as ``plan``, plus a non-empty ``goals`` sequence of candidate
138	  endpoint coordinates. It returns one deterministic minimum-cost route to
139	  any of the candidates, in the same result structure as ``plan``; the
140	  path's last point is the winning endpoint.
141	- The grid, costs, trace, dynamic-blocked and budget checks run in
142	  ``plan``'s order with the same exception types; ``goals`` takes
143	  ``goal``'s position in that sequence. The outer value must be a
144	  sequence: strings, bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise
145	  ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each endpoint
146	  follows the coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or
147	  coordinate types raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and
148	  endpoints on static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated candidates
149	  merge, so the input ordering never changes any result.
150	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, no waiting, no revisits, the
151	  persistent last frame and the entering-cell cost accumulation. A
152	  candidate blocked by the dynamic frame at the time a particular route
153	  arrives is not rejected up front (its coordinate is statically valid);
154	  that arrival is simply infeasible for that route's time frame while
155	  other arrival times still compete.
156	- Total ``cost`` decides; ties compare the endpoint coordinate ``(x, y)``
157	  lexicographically, then the complete coordinate path lexicographically.
158	  As in dynamic ``plan``, routes reaching the same cell through different
159	  coordinate histories are distinct states and are never merged, so the
160	  traversal is a best-first walk of the feasible route tree; expansion
161	  order and the trace never depend on goal order, the blocked sets or
162	  in-frame iteration order. A budget never replaces an already determined
163	  better route with a worse one.
164	- When no endpoint is reachable, ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``. With a
165	  budget the ``status`` field follows the same ``"found"``,
166	  ``"unreachable"`` and ``"budget_exhausted"`` rules, and ``trace`` only
167	  records actually closed nodes: coordinate pairs in static mode and
168	  ``(x, y, t)`` triples in dynamic mode. A ``goals`` containing ``start``
169	  yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same start-equals-goal
170	  and zero-budget rules as ``plan``. A successful path verifies offline in
171	  ``replay`` when its last point is passed as ``goal``, with the same cost
172	  and step count.
173	
174	Top-k planning (``plan_k``):
175	- ``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
176	  dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None)`` returns
177	  several distinct feasible routes on the same grid in one call. It
178	  first performs exactly ``plan``'s shared validation for the
179	  dimensions, coordinates, static obstacles, positive integer cost
180	  matrix and dynamic frames (including the frame-0 start check), and
181	  only then checks ``k``: a non-bool positive integer is required,
182	  wrong types raise ``TypeError`` and non-positive values raise
183	  ``ValueError``. The optional ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost``
184	  limits are checked after all of that (the ``k`` check included),
185	  still before the search starts, with the same non-negative,
186	  non-bool integer rules ``plan`` uses (other types raise
187	  ``TypeError``, negative values raise ``ValueError``). Every error is
188	  decided before the search starts, and ``plan_k`` accepts no
189	  ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` argument.
190	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, the zero start cost, the
191	  entering-cell cost accumulation, the persistent last frame, the ban on
192	  waiting in place and on repeated coordinates, and the static/frame
193	  feasibility rules. Routes that reach the same cell through different
194	  coordinate histories are distinct candidates and are never merged, in
195	  both static and dynamic mode, so different complete coordinate
196	  sequences always remain separate results.
197	- It returns ``{"paths": [...], "costs": [...], "expanded": int}``: at
198	  most ``k`` unique complete routes ordered by ascending total cost and,
199	  on ties, by the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate
200	  sequence; ``costs`` corresponds to ``paths`` entry by entry. The first
201	  entry is the route ``plan`` would return. When no route is feasible
202	  both lists are empty and ``expanded`` still reports the route
203	  candidates actually closed to determine the answer: one count per
204	  complete history, and never counting a candidate filtered at
205	  generation or left pending. The traversal stops the moment the k-th
206	  goal route has been closed, so a small k closes strictly fewer
207	  candidates than a larger one. ``start == goal`` yields only the
208	  single-point zero-cost route, with one expansion. Every returned route
209	  verifies offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count, in
210	  both static and dynamic mode; the result never depends on obstacle-set
211	  iteration order, in-frame coordinate order or the traversal order.
212	- ``max_cost`` caps a route's accumulated entering-cell cost exactly as
213	  in ``plan``: the start still costs 0, a candidate exactly at the
214	  limit still competes and a candidate whose accumulated cost would
215	  exceed it is discarded the moment it is generated. It never changes
216	  the tie-break between legal routes. ``max_expanded`` caps the number
217	  of complete route candidates actually closed (exactly what
218	  ``expanded`` counts); once the limit is reached no further candidate
219	  is closed, and the limit only ever truncates the traversal -- it can
220	  never replace an already determined higher-ranked route. When either
221	  limit is provided the result additionally carries ``status``:
222	  ``"found"`` when all ``k`` routes were closed or the search exhausted
223	  naturally with at least one route; ``"budget_exhausted"`` when fewer
224	  than ``k`` routes were found and the budget stopped the search while
225	  candidates were still pending (this wins when both limits fire);
226	  ``"cost_exhausted"`` when fewer than ``k`` routes were found, no
227	  budget stop occurred and at least one candidate was discarded for the
228	  cost limit; ``"unreachable"`` when no route exists with neither a
229	  budget stop nor a cost discard. The routes already closed (and their
230	  costs, in rank order) are still returned when a limit ends the search
231	  early, as empty lists when none were found, and ``expanded`` is the
232	  actual closed count. Omitting both limits keeps every legacy key and
233	  value exactly unchanged.
234	
235	Batch planning (``plan_batch``):
236	- ``plan_batch(width, height, blocked, requests, costs=None,
237	  trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
238	  max_cost=None)`` answers several independent single-goal queries on
239	  one shared grid in a single call. It returns ``{"results": [...]}``
240	  with exactly the result ``plan`` would return for each query, in the
241	  order of ``requests``; duplicate requests are kept and each gets its
242	  own result.
243	- The shared arguments are validated with ``plan``'s rules and order,
244	  with ``requests`` taking the position of ``start``/``goal`` in that
245	  sequence. ``requests`` must be a non-empty sequence: ``None``,
246	  strings, bytes and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError`` and an
247	  empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each element must be a
248	  two-element sequence ``[start, goal]`` of grid coordinates: element
249	  shape or coordinate type failures raise ``TypeError``; out-of-bounds
250	  coordinates, endpoints on static obstacles and a start blocked at
251	  dynamic frame 0 raise ``ValueError``. Every check is decided before
252	  any search starts, so an invalid batch never returns partial results.
253	- Each query is an independent ``plan`` search over the shared grid:
254	  ``path``, ``cost`` and ``expanded`` are produced per request, and the
255	  ``max_expanded`` budget and the ``max_cost`` limit apply per query
256	  with no state shared across queries. ``trace``, ``status``,
257	  ``expanded_nodes``, ``checkpoint``, dynamic frames, ``start == goal``,
258	  unreachable and ``cost_exhausted`` results all follow ``plan``
259	  exactly, and a returned ``checkpoint`` can be handed to ``resume``
260	  directly. A successful path ends at its request's goal and verifies
261	  offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count. The result
262	  never depends on obstacle-set iteration order, in-frame coordinate
263	  order or the permutation of ``requests``.
264	
265	Multi-start planning (``plan_multi_start``):
266	- ``plan_multi_start(width, height, blocked, starts, goal, costs=None,
267	  trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
268	  max_cost=None)`` plans from several candidate starts to one shared
269	  goal in a single call and returns one deterministic route, in exactly
270	  the result structure of ``plan``; the path begins at the winning start
271	  and ends at ``goal``. ``starts`` takes ``start``'s position in
272	  ``plan``'s validation sequence and every shared check keeps its order,
273	  exception type and message boundary.
274	- ``starts`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates: ``None``,
275	  strings, bytes and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError`` and an
276	  empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each start follows the
277	  coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or coordinate types
278	  raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and starts on static
279	  obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated starts merge and the tuple is
280	  sorted, so the input ordering never changes any result. A start
281	  blocked by dynamic frame 0 raises ``ValueError``; every check runs
282	  before the search starts.
283	- In static mode every start is a ``g == 0`` root and each coordinate is
284	  closed at most once: a cell keeps only its best known ``(cost, path)``
285	  pair (smallest accumulated entering-cell cost, then the
286	  lexicographically smallest complete coordinate sequence -- an ordering
287	  preserved under common extensions, so a dominated candidate can never
288	  win later). In dynamic mode the persistent last frame, the ban on
289	  waiting and on repeated coordinates apply, and routes reaching the
290	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
291	  states that are never merged.
292	- The winning route has the smallest total ``cost``; ties are decided by
293	  the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate path, so the result
294	  never depends on the input order of ``starts``. Expansion order is f,
295	  then h, then ``(x, y)`` (plus ``t`` in dynamic mode), and finally the
296	  complete path. ``cost`` counts only the cells entered (the winning
297	  start costs 0); ``expanded`` counts only closed candidates; when no
298	  route exists ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``.
299	- With ``trace=True`` static mode records the unique coordinate closing
300	  sequence and dynamic mode the ``(x, y, t)`` closing sequence, and
301	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. A ``starts`` entry equal to
302	  ``goal`` yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same
303	  start-equals-goal and zero-budget rules as ``plan``.
304	- ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost`` follow ``plan``'s ``status`` and
305	  budget-priority rules: a candidate whose accumulated cost would
306	  exceed ``max_cost`` is discarded without counting toward ``expanded``,
307	  and neither limit ever changes the unlimited route or the tie-breaks.
308	  With ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop returns a JSON-serializable
309	  checkpoint recording the sorted starts, the grid constraints, the
310	  dynamic frames, the cost limit when one was provided and the complete
311	  pending state; ``resume`` continues it with the cumulative-budget,
312	  no-double-counting and only-budget-exhausted-snapshots rules of the
313	  other planners, and invalid checkpoints follow ``resume``'s usual
314	  ``TypeError``/``ValueError`` boundaries.
315	
316	Snapshots and resumable planning (``snapshot`` and ``resume``):
317	- ``plan`` and ``plan_any`` accept a final ``snapshot=False`` option.
318	  Omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps every key, value, exception type,
319	  validation order, tie-break, unreachable result and trace of the
320	  previous behavior untouched. A non-bool ``snapshot`` raises
321	  ``TypeError`` after all existing checks (the ``max_expanded`` validation
322	  included) and before the search starts.
323	- With ``snapshot=True``, a search that stops because ``max_expanded``
324	  was reached (``status == "budget_exhausted"``) additionally returns
325	  ``checkpoint``: a fully JSON-serializable snapshot of the planner state.
326	  Results that already found the goal or proved it unreachable never
327	  carry the field.
328	- The checkpoint records the snapshot version, the planner kind, the
329	  normalized grid constraints (dimensions, obstacles, start, goal or
330	  candidate goals, costs, dynamic frames and the cost limit when one was
331	  provided), the closed-node count, the
332	  trace recorded so far and the complete pending-candidate state. Every
333	  set-derived list is stored sorted, so neither obstacle-set iteration
334	  order, goal order nor in-frame coordinate order influences the
335	  checkpoint's keys or values. A caller may store it as-is and hand it
336	  back to ``resume`` later.
337	- ``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)`` continues the very same
338	  deterministic search described by the snapshot. ``max_expanded`` keeps
339	  its cumulative meaning: the total number of nodes that may be closed
340	  counted from the original start, so a limit not greater than the
341	  already closed count closes nothing more. The result is equivalent to
342	  one uninterrupted call with the same cumulative budget: ``path``,
343	  ``cost``, ``expanded``, ``status`` (present exactly when
344	  ``max_expanded`` is given) and ``expanded_nodes`` (always present in
345	  resume results; coordinate pairs in static mode, ``(x, y, t)`` triples
346	  in dynamic mode) all match, and repeated resumes never count an already
347	  closed node twice.
348	- When a resumed search reaches the budget again its result carries a
349	  fresh ``checkpoint`` that can be resumed in turn; ``found`` and
350	  ``unreachable`` results omit it. A successful resumed ``path`` verifies
351	  in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count.
352	- Validation: a checkpoint that is not an object, has missing required
353	  fields or wrongly typed fields raises ``TypeError``; an unsupported
354	  snapshot version or planner kind, grid constraints that violate the
355	  usual ``plan`` rules (obstacles, endpoints, costs, dynamic frames) or
356	  an internally inconsistent state raise ``ValueError``. Every check is
357	  decided before any searching, and ``resume``'s ``max_expanded`` follows
358	  the same non-negative-integer rules as ``plan``'s.
359	
360	Offline replay (``replay``):
361	- ``replay`` re-checks a saved candidate path without running any search;
362	  it never returns ``expanded`` or ``expanded_nodes``. It accepts the same
363	  grid arguments as ``plan`` (no ``trace``) plus ``path``.
364	- The grid arguments are validated with exactly the public ``plan``
365	  checks, and all of them run before the path is judged, so the same
366	  malformed grid inputs raise the same ``TypeError``/``ValueError``.
367	- ``path`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates; strings,
368	  bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, as do
369	  elements that are not exactly two integers. Coordinates outside the
370	  grid raise ``ValueError``.
371	- A structurally valid but semantically invalid path does not raise: it
372	  returns ``{"valid": False, "cost": None, "steps": None}`` with no
373	  partial accumulation. Invalid means: not beginning at ``start``, not
374	  ending at ``goal``, visiting a static obstacle, visiting a cell blocked
375	  by frame ``t`` at path index ``t`` (the last frame persists for later
376	  indices; omitted/empty ``dynamic_blocked`` means static-only checks),
377	  non-four-neighbor adjacency, repeated coordinates, or extra points when
378	  ``start == goal``.
379	- A valid path returns ``{"valid": True, "cost": int, "steps": int}``
380	  where ``steps == len(path) - 1`` and ``cost`` is recomputed with the
381	  same entering-cell rule ``plan`` uses (sum of the costs of the cells
382	  entered; unit costs without ``costs``; the start cell is never
383	  counted), so it equals the cost ``plan`` assigns to that same path.
384	- ``diagnose`` defaults to false; omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps
385	  every key, value, exception type and validation order identical. A
386	  non-bool ``diagnose`` raises ``TypeError`` after all grid checks
387	  (including the frame-0 check) and before the path structure is
388	  inspected. With ``diagnose=True`` both results additionally carry
389	  ``error`` and ``error_index``: ``None``/``None`` for a valid path, and
390	  for an invalid one a single error code plus the zero-based index of
391	  the first offending element, with ``cost``/``steps`` still ``None``.
392	  The codes, in fixed precedence order, are ``start_mismatch`` (index
393	  0), ``goal_mismatch`` (index of the last element),
394	  ``start_goal_extra`` (index 1), ``repeated_coordinate`` (the second
395	  occurrence), ``non_adjacent`` (the later element of the pair),
396	  ``static_blocked`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` (the offending element);
397	  ties resolve to the earliest rule in this list and no partial cost is
398	  ever returned.
399	
400	Distance field (``distance_field``):
401	- ``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None,
402	  trace=False)`` is an offline analysis entry point for the static grid:
403	  it accepts only the dimensions, the static obstacles, a single goal and
404	  optionally ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no
405	  search budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option. The dimensions,
406	  goal coordinate, obstacle and costs checks (structure, integer types,
407	  bounds, duplicate merging, goal-on-obstacle) follow ``plan``'s public
408	  rules and order for those shared arguments and all run before the
409	  search starts; ``trace`` must be a bool (``TypeError`` otherwise).
410	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "expanded": int}`` where ``distances``
411	  is a height-by-width matrix indexed ``distances[y][x]``: ``None`` for
412	  obstacles and for cells that cannot reach the goal, ``0`` for the goal
413	  itself, and for every other reachable cell the minimum sum of the
414	  entering-cell costs along a four-neighborhood route from that cell to
415	  the goal (unit steps without ``costs``; with ``costs`` each move adds
416	  the cost of the cell entered, exactly as ``plan`` accumulates ``cost``,
417	  so a reachable ``plan`` start yields the same value ``plan`` reports
418	  as ``cost``). No reachable distance is ever negative and the matrix
419	  always matches the grid dimensions; the result is JSON-serializable.
420	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the reachable cells determined and closed
421	  once each, the goal included. The closing order is fully specified:
422	  smallest current distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate in
423	  lexicographic order, so neither the obstacle-set iteration order nor
424	  the costs layout traversal influences the matrix, the count or the
425	  trace. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally carries
426	  ``expanded_nodes``, the coordinate pairs in that closing order, and
427	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``; the field is omitted entirely
428	  when ``trace`` is false or omitted.
429	
430	Multi-goal distance field (``distance_field_any``):
431	- ``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
432	  trace=False)`` is the multi-goal counterpart of ``distance_field``:
433	  one offline analysis returns the minimum-cost field to any of the
434	  candidate endpoints in a single pass. It accepts only the dimensions,
435	  the static obstacles, a non-empty ``goals`` sequence and optionally
436	  ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no search
437	  budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option, and it never produces a
438	  ``status`` field. The dimensions, obstacles, costs and trace checks
439	  follow ``distance_field``'s public rules and order, and ``goals`` is
440	  validated exactly like ``plan_any``'s: ``None``, strings, bytes and
441	  other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, an empty sequence raises
442	  ``ValueError``, elements that are not exactly two non-bool integers
443	  raise ``TypeError``, and out-of-bounds coordinates or endpoints on
444	  static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. The goals checks occupy
445	  ``goal``'s position in ``distance_field``'s validation sequence,
446	  duplicates merge, and every check runs before the search starts, so
447	  the input permutation never changes any result.
448	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "targets": ..., "expanded": int}``.
449	  ``distances`` is the same height-by-width matrix as
450	  ``distance_field``: ``None`` for obstacles and for cells that cannot
451	  reach any endpoint, ``0`` for every endpoint, and otherwise the
452	  minimum over the endpoints of the accumulated entering-cell cost
453	  along a four-neighborhood route (unit steps without ``costs``; with
454	  ``costs`` each move adds the cost of the cell entered, the start
455	  cell's own cost never counted, exactly as ``plan``/``plan_any`` and
456	  ``distance_field`` accumulate). A reachable ``plan_any`` start yields
457	  the same value ``plan_any`` reports as ``cost``.
458	- ``targets`` is a matrix of the same shape: a reachable cell records
459	  the coordinate tuple of the endpoint that wins it, every other
460	  position is ``None`` (obstacles and unreachable cells, exactly where
461	  ``distances`` is ``None``); endpoints record themselves. When several
462	  endpoints tie at the same minimum distance the winner is the endpoint
463	  with the lexicographically smallest ``(x, y)`` coordinate, so the
464	  choice never depends on goal order. The whole result is
465	  JSON-serializable.
466	- ``expanded`` counts every reachable cell closed for the first time,
467	  all endpoints included, exactly once each. The closing order is
468	  smallest distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate
469	  lexicographically. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally
470	  carries ``expanded_nodes`` -- the coordinate pairs in that order,
471	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)`` -- and the key is omitted
472	  entirely when ``trace`` is false or omitted.
473	
474	Validation (all performed before the search starts):
475	- ``width``/``height`` must be positive integers.
476	- ``start``, ``goal`` and every entry of ``blocked`` must be grid
477	  coordinates: sequences of exactly two integers (tuples, lists, etc.),
478	  normalized to tuples.
479	- ``goals`` (``plan_any`` and ``distance_field_any``) must be a
480	  non-empty sequence of grid coordinates following the same rules,
481	  normalized, deduplicated and order-independent.
482	- ``requests`` (``plan_batch``) must be a non-empty sequence of
483	  two-element ``[start, goal]`` coordinate pairs following the same
484	  coordinate rules, with the input order and duplicates preserved.
485	- ``costs`` may be omitted or ``None`` (unit costs). Otherwise it must be a
486	  sequence of ``height`` rows, each a sequence of ``width`` positive
487	  integers; strings/bytes, non-integer cells and booleans are rejected.
488	- ``trace`` must be a bool; non-bool values raise ``TypeError``.
489	- Type or structure violations raise ``TypeError``; non-positive
490	  dimensions, out-of-bounds coordinates, endpoints on obstacles, wrong
491	  matrix shape, or non-positive cell costs raise ``ValueError``.
492	- Duplicate blocked cells are merged without changing the result.
493	"""

510	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

513	def _validate_dimension(value, name):
514	    if not _is_int(value):
515	        raise TypeError(
516	            f"{name} must be an int, got {type(value).__name__}"
517	        )
518	    if value <= 0:
519	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a positive integer, got {value}")

523	def _normalize_point(value, name):
524	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, Sequence):
525	        raise TypeError(
526	            f"{name} must be a sequence of two integers, "
527	            f"got {type(value).__name__}"
528	        )
529	    if len(value) != 2:
530	        raise TypeError(
531	            f"{name} must contain exactly two coordinates, got {len(value)}"
532	        )
533	    x, y = value[0], value[1]
534	    if not _is_int(x) or not _is_int(y):
535	        raise TypeError(f"{name} coordinates must be integers, got {value!r}")

539	def _check_bounds(point, width, height, name):
540	    x, y = point
541	    if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height):
542	        raise ValueError(
543	            f"{name} {point} is outside the {width}x{height} grid"
544	        )

547	def _normalize_blocked(blocked, width, height):
548	    if isinstance(blocked, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(blocked, Iterable):
549	        raise TypeError(
550	            f"blocked must be an iterable of grid coordinates, "
551	            f"got {type(blocked).__name__}"
552	        )
553	    cells = set()
554	    for index, item in enumerate(blocked):
555	        name = f"blocked[{index}]"
556	        point = _normalize_point(item, name)
557	        _check_bounds(point, width, height, name)
558	        cells.add(point)  # duplicates merge into one cell
559	    return cells

562	def _normalize_costs(costs, width, height):
563	    if costs is None:
564	        return None  # unit step cost
565	    if isinstance(costs, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(costs, Sequence):
566	        raise TypeError(
567	            f"costs must be a height-by-width matrix of positive integers, "
568	            f"got {type(costs).__name__}"
569	        )
570	    if len(costs) != height:
571	        raise ValueError(
572	            f"costs must have exactly {height} rows, got {len(costs)}"
573	        )
574	    rows = []
575	    for y, row in enumerate(costs):
576	        if isinstance(row, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(row, Sequence):
577	            raise TypeError(
578	                f"costs[{y}] must be a sequence of {width} positive "
579	                f"integers, got {type(row).__name__}"
580	            )
581	        if len(row) != width:
582	            raise ValueError(
583	                f"costs[{y}] must have exactly {width} cells, "
584	                f"got {len(row)}"
585	            )
586	        parsed = []
587	        for x, cell in enumerate(row):
588	            if not _is_int(cell):
589	                raise TypeError(
590	                    f"costs[{y}][{x}] must be an int, "
591	                    f"got {type(cell).__name__}"
592	                )
593	            if cell <= 0:
594	                raise ValueError(
595	                    f"costs[{y}][{x}] must be a positive integer, "
596	                    f"got {cell}"
597	                )
598	            parsed.append(cell)
599	        rows.append(tuple(parsed))
600	    return tuple(rows)

603	def _normalize_dynamic_blocked(dynamic_blocked, width, height):
604	    if dynamic_blocked is None:
605	        return None  # dynamic mode disabled
606	    if isinstance(dynamic_blocked, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(
607	        dynamic_blocked, Sequence
608	    ):
609	        raise TypeError(
610	            f"dynamic_blocked must be a sequence of frames, "
611	            f"got {type(dynamic_blocked).__name__}"
612	        )
613	    if len(dynamic_blocked) == 0:
614	        return None  # no frames: equivalent to not provided
615	    frames = []
616	    for t, frame in enumerate(dynamic_blocked):
617	        if isinstance(frame, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(frame, Iterable):
618	            raise TypeError(
619	                f"dynamic_blocked[{t}] must be an iterable of grid "
620	                f"coordinates, got {type(frame).__name__}"
621	            )
622	        cells = set()
623	        for index, item in enumerate(frame):
624	            name = f"dynamic_blocked[{t}][{index}]"
625	            point = _normalize_point(item, name)
626	            _check_bounds(point, width, height, name)
627	            cells.add(point)  # duplicates merge into one cell
628	        frames.append(frozenset(cells))
629	    return frames

650	def _normalize_goals(goals):
651	    # ``goals`` is the plan_any counterpart of ``plan``'s single ``goal``.
652	    # This performs the outer/structure pass in exactly the position where
653	    # ``plan`` structurally normalizes ``goal``: strings, bytes, ``None``
654	    # and other non-sequences are ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence is a
655	    # ``ValueError``; every element is normalized to a coordinate tuple
656	    # (element shape/coordinate type failures are ``TypeError``). Bounds and
657	    # obstacle checks follow in ``plan_any`` at the same relative positions
658	    # ``plan`` uses for its single goal. Duplicates merge and the tuple is
659	    # sorted so the input order never affects the result.
660	    if (goals is None or isinstance(goals, (str, bytes))
661	            or not isinstance(goals, Sequence)):
662	        raise TypeError(
663	            f"goals must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates, "
664	            f"got {type(goals).__name__}"
665	        )
666	    if len(goals) == 0:
667	        raise ValueError("goals must contain at least one candidate endpoint")
668	    points = set()
669	    for index, item in enumerate(goals):
670	        point = _normalize_point(item, f"goals[{index}]")
671	        points.add(point)
672	    return tuple(sorted(points))

702	    # ``requests`` is the plan_batch counterpart of ``plan``'s
703	    # ``start``/``goal`` pair. This performs the outer/structure pass in
704	    # exactly the position where ``plan`` structurally normalizes its
705	    # endpoints: strings, bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences are
706	    # ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence is a ``ValueError``. Every
707	    # element must be a [start, goal] pair of grid coordinates (element
708	    # shape or coordinate type failures are ``TypeError``); bounds and

710	    # positions ``plan`` uses for its endpoints. The input order and
711	    # duplicate requests are preserved: every element gets its own

715	        raise TypeError(
716	            f"requests must be a non-empty sequence of [start, goal] "
717	            f"coordinate pairs, got {type(requests).__name__}"
718	        )
719	    if len(requests) == 0:
720	        raise ValueError("requests must contain at least one query")
721	    pairs = []
722	    for index, item in enumerate(requests):
723	        name = f"requests[{index}]"
724	        if isinstance(item, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(item, Sequence):
725	            raise TypeError(
726	                f"{name} must be a [start, goal] pair of grid "
727	                f"coordinates, got {type(item).__name__}"
728	            )
729	        if len(item) != 2:
730	            raise TypeError(
731	                f"{name} must contain exactly two coordinates, "
732	                f"got {len(item)}"
733	            )
734	        start = _normalize_point(item[0], f"{name} start")
735	        goal = _normalize_point(item[1], f"{name} goal")
736	        pairs.append((start, goal))
737	    return pairs

791	def _search_static(width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, trace,
792	                   max_expanded, max_cost=None, snapshot=False, state=None):
793	    """Classic static-grid A* (the ``plan`` search without frames).
794	
795	    Cells are merged by coordinate: the best known ``g`` per cell is kept
796	    in ``g_score``, stale heap entries are skipped, and ``came_from``
797	    reconstructs the cheapest route once the goal is closed. With
798	    ``max_cost`` a candidate whose accumulated entering-cell cost would
799	    exceed the limit is discarded instead of queued, and the search
800	    remembers whether any discard happened (``cost_limited``) so a
801	    failure can be reported as ``cost_exhausted``; the flag is part of
802	    the snapshot state so a resumed search stays equivalent to one
803	    uninterrupted call. With
804	    ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop additionally returns a checkpoint of
805	    the complete search state; ``state`` carries such a snapshot back in
806	    so ``resume`` continues the identical traversal. The snapshot needs
807	    the trace even when the caller did not ask for it, so nodes are
808	    recorded whenever ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` is true.
809	    """
810	
811	    def heuristic(point):
812	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
813	
814	    def step_cost(point):
815	        # Cost of entering ``point``; the start cell is never entered.
816	        if costs is None:
817	            return 1
818	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]
819	
820	    if state is None:
821	        # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, point): the first four fields give
822	        # a total, input-order-independent ordering, so the point itself
823	        # is never compared.
824	        h0 = heuristic(start)
825	        open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], start)]
826	        came_from = {}
827	        g_score = {start: 0}
828	        closed = set()
829	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
830	        cost_limited = False
831	    else:
832	        open_heap = state["open"]
833	        came_from = state["came_from"]
834	        g_score = state["g_score"]
835	        closed = state["closed"]
836	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
837	        cost_limited = state["cost_limited"]
838	    budget_stop = False
839	    has_status = max_expanded is not None or max_cost is not None
840	
841	    while open_heap:
842	        entry = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
843	        current = entry[4]
844	        if current in closed:
845	            continue  # stale heap entry; already closed with its best g
846	        if max_expanded is not None and len(closed) >= max_expanded:
847	            # A live candidate remains but the budget is spent; close
848	            # nothing more (this also covers start == goal with a zero
849	            # budget: no node is closed and no start is fabricated). The
850	            # popped candidate was already removed from the heap, so for a
